featured_reviews.review_text:
Babu Vada pav is essentially a takeaway snack joint on the street; they have been operating in that location for decades. They transformed from a street food vendor on a wheeled cart to a takeaway snack joint.

There is no seating available so basically you can order a TAKEAWAY or have it on a disposable plate.

It's one of the "go-to" places for snacks in a 10 kilometre radius; Quality & is taste is a function of who's making the vada pav batter or batata bhaji ; salt / green chilli/ garlic proportions vary from time to time.

Likewise perception of service can also vary depending on who's on the service side of the counter or the type of crowd at peak hours

In addition to their Vada Pav,  Patti Samosa and Kothimbir Vadi are also to be savoured once. Sabudana vada is also good going by reviews of many esteemed  local guides

The type of snacks served uses copious amounts of garlic without which vada cannot get its taste; so if you are finicky about not having garlic for whatever reasons you may have to think twice before consuming

One of their dry chutneys also contains dry coconut and peanut in addition to garlic ; if you have allergies be aware of them before consuming

Parking is available on alternate sides of the streets on odd days and even days , but the proximity to street corners and bus stops make it a challenging task ; during off peak hours parking is available but the snacks may not be piping hot at that time.

There is also a school nearby so it can be chaotic during school rush hours or in the evening between 1730 - 1930 due to peak station going traffic

They do not sell any beverages but there is a sugarcane juice stall, tea stall nearby and several stores where one can buy bottled water or cold beverages.

Summarily definitely a decent place to have a small snack and if you are a regular you'd know when to visit them

featured_reviews.name: Aniket
featured_reviews.review_text:
Anand on Hanuman Road, Vile Parle East has quickly become one of our regular go-to places simply because of both convenience and quality. Being very close to our home, we find ourselves visiting quite often, and the experience has consistently been satisfying. The restaurant offers a great mix of traditional South Indian dishes along with popular Mumbai-style snacks, which makes it a perfect spot whether you are in the mood for a classic dosa or a typical Mumbai indulgence like pav bhaji or grilled sandwiches. Their dosas are crisp and flavorful, the chutneys are fresh, and the pav bhaji has that authentic Mumbai taste without being overly spicy or greasy. The grilled sandwich is another favorite — well-stuffed and nicely toasted.

Service is fast, the staff is polite, and food arrives quicker than you expect, which is a big plus especially during busy hours. The seating area is slightly limited, so at peak times you might have to wait a bit or adjust accordingly. Parking can sometimes be a bit of a hustle, particularly during evenings and weekends, but if you’re walking in from the neighborhood, it’s not an issue at all.

Overall, Anand is a reliable, tasty, and well-priced option for both South Indian and Mumbai-style comfort food. Recommended!

featured_reviews.name: shrikant Sharma
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Anand Stall with my wife and father-in-law and was extremely disappointed with the overall experience.

The quality of the famous Jini Dosa has noticeably declined compared to what Anand Stall used to serve at its previous location.

What was even more disappointing was the service. The staff did not seem to note down orders and instead tried to remember everything. As a result, one of the items we had ordered was never prepared. When I enquired about it, the response from the staff was simply, “I forgot.”

When I asked them to cancel the item since we had already waited long enough, they suddenly claimed that it was “almost ready.” It appeared to be an attempt to buy more time rather than an honest update, as the item clearly had not been prepared.

The most unacceptable part of the visit was the staff’s attitude. When my father-in-law raised concerns about the service and behaviour, some staff members were laughing instead of apologizing or showing any concern. Such behaviour towards customers, especially senior citizens, is highly disrespectful and unprofessional.

I also noticed staff being rude to guests who were arriving and looking for seats. Instead of politely explaining the waiting situation, they were bluntly told to sit outside because there was no space available.

Good food can attract customers once, but courteous service and respect are what bring them back. Unfortunately, Anand Stall failed on both counts during our visit. I hope the management takes customer feedback seriously and works on improving both food taste and staff behaviour.

Sharma Bhelpuri House in Vile Parle East Market is truly an iconic food destination and a landmark for chat lovers in the locality. It is popularly believed to be Sachin Tendulkar’s favourite chat place, and the walls proudly display photographs of occasions where Sharma Bhelpuri had set up counters at Sachin’s residence for Arjun Tendulkar’s birthday celebrations. This association alone tells you how special and loved this place is by generations of Parle residents.

Evenings here are vibrant, with crowds lining up to enjoy their famous chat items. Their Panipuri is absolutely outstanding—crisp puris, perfectly balanced spicy-sweet water, and fresh filling. It’s no surprise that the Panipuri counter is almost always surrounded by eager customers. Other must-try items include their Dahi Puri, Sevpuri, Bhelpuri, and the very popular Radha Patties, each prepared with consistent quality and delicious taste.

They do offer indoor seating, though it is somewhat limited due to their popularity. Despite the rush, service is quick, efficient, and well-managed. The hygiene and freshness they maintain while serving such fast-paced orders is genuinely commendable.

My personal favourite here is the Sevpuri—bursting with flavour and incredibly satisfying. If you are anywhere near Vile Parle East Market, this place is a must-visit for some delightful, authentic chat that never disappoints. Highly recommended!

I recently visited Garde Manger Café in Vile Parle East, and while the food was enjoyable, the overall experience was far from satisfying.

Parking:
As with many cafés in this area, there is no dedicated parking available. Visitors traveling by car or bike should be prepared to look around for legal street parking — not very convenient.

Seating & Ambience:
The café offers both indoor and outdoor seating, but the space feels very tight and congested. The tables are extremely small — if you’re planning to order multiple dishes, you’ll struggle to fit everything on the table at once. It gets uncomfortable quickly.

Also, the tables are placed too close to each other, and when the café is full, the noise levels can be overwhelming. During our visit, there was a loud group nearby, and due to the cramped layout, it was hard to have a peaceful conversation or enjoy our food.

Service:
The service was slow and poorly coordinated. We ordered hummus with pita bread, and although we had already finished most of our meal, the pita bread hadn’t arrived. When we followed up, it was clear from the staff’s expressions that they had forgotten to place the order. It eventually arrived after a wait of 30+ minutes, which really disrupted the flow of our meal.

Food:
On the positive side, the food was genuinely good — tasty and fresh. The flavors were spot on, and if I had to rate just the food, I’d give it a thumbs-up.

⸻

Final Thoughts:
While the food is worth trying, the lack of space, poor service, and noisy environment took away from what could have been a nice café experience. I hope the management considers expanding the space and training the staff better to handle orders and communication.

⭐☆☆☆☆ A Masterclass in Incompetence — KFC T2 Mumbai Airport

I have traveled across dozens of countries and eaten at hundreds of airports. Never — and I mean never — have I witnessed such a breathtaking display of collective indifference as I did at KFC, Terminal 2, Mumbai Airport.

Let me paint you a picture: 10 staff members on duty. Zero customers being served. Not because there was no work to do — my food was sitting right there on the counter, getting cold, in plain sight. Instead, your entire team had apparently decided that this was the perfect moment for a staff social gathering, huddled together chatting 3 meters away from my order like they were at a house party.

I stood there. Waiting. Watching my food go cold. I even had the audacity to say, "Excuse me, my food is right there." The response? A glance, a shrug, and back to the conversation. I was dismissed like an inconvenience in a restaurant I was paying to eat at.

Eventually — after what felt like a minor eternity — I had to literally point at each individual item on the counter just to get someone to hand it to me. At an airport. Where time is everything.

This isn't a staffing problem. This is a management catastrophe. Where is the supervisor? Where is the accountability? How is it possible that with 10 employees present, a single customer cannot get served without staging a one-man intervention?

Mumbai Airport T2 food court already sets a remarkably low bar — but KFC has somehow managed to limbo under it. If you value your time, your sanity, or even lukewarm food, walk past this place and don't look back.

To KFC management: your cameras saw everything. Go check them. Then ask yourselves why your team treats paying customers like an interruption to their social life.

Absolutely disgraceful. Do better — or don't operate at all.

EDIT: Half an hour later, I don't feel so well in the stomach...
